comparison: Both evaluate ThT as a membrane potential reporter (C36, C41, C43). OpenEval finds the methodological validation SUPPORTED by multiple dyes and controls. Peer reviewers find it UNSUPPORTED, fundamentally challenging whether ThT acts as a Nernstian dye in E. coli and noting incomplete controls and contradictions with published work.

Both address synchronized membrane potential dynamics and blue light response (C4, C5, C32, C37). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by ThT fluorescence data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether dynamics are actually blue light-induced and noting the absence of critical negative controls (measurements without blue light).

Both evaluate wavefront propagation claims (C49-C54). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by time-lapse microscopy showing bidirectional wavefront movement. Peer reviewers find UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating they cannot identify traveling wavefronts in the data and observe cells brightening in tandem rather than propagating signals.

Both assess mechanosensitive channel roles (C6, C33, C98, C133). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by deletion experiments showing loss of spiking dynamics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the claim is misleading as MS channels ablate all dynamics rather than specifically affecting the first peak, and questioning blue light-independent effects.

Both evaluate Kch channel's role in the second peak (C7, C66-C69, C123-C124). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by deletion/complementation experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional controls (valinomycin) and noting the complementation data needs better temporal resolution for convincing validation.

Both assess protective role claims via LiveDead assay (C77-C80, C144). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by PI staining showing ~4.5-fold difference. Peer reviewers find UNSUPPORTED, noting absence of critical negative controls (PI staining without blue light, experiments without ThT) and concerns about PI uptake confounds.

Both evaluate potassium measurements (C75-C76). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by IPG-4 indicator showing temporal correlation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting kinetic discrepancies between potassium and ThT peaks (potassium rises minutes earlier) and questioning consistency with the Kch model.

Both assess catalase experiments linking ROS to second peak (C81-C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting multiple possible interpretations including catalase reducing ThT photobleaching, and stating the experiment doesn't demonstrate that membrane potential fluctuations help cells respond to stress.

Both evaluate the Hodgkin-Huxley model predictions (C85, C88-C92, C128-C129). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by model matching experimental data. Peer reviewers find UNSUPPORTED, extensively critiquing the lack of empirical basis for model parameters (why n^4, gqz^4 forms) and noting the model should be compared to single-cell rather than biofilm data.

Both assess ABFDF model predictions of anomalous exponents and critical size (C99, C104, C106, C108-C109, C118, C130). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by agreement between simulation and experiment. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting discrepancies in plateau heights, unconvincing similarity in kinetics, and that wavefront measurements are unclear since wavefronts aren't evident in videos.

Both evaluate density-dependent synchronization (C45-C47, C55-C57, C84, C116). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by quantitative measurements showing reduced latency with decreased distance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting histograms, statistical tests, and noting that overlaid normalized traces make comparisons difficult to evaluate.

Both assess irradiance threshold effects (C71-C74, C138). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by systematic experiments identifying threshold for second peak. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that slower dynamics at lower irradiance may show second peaks with extended measurement time, and that limited temporal resolution challenges interpretation.

Both address ThT toxicity/growth effects (C48). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by growth curves. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that growth curves don't address photodynamic toxicity during actual experimental conditions and requesting PI staining experiments with/without ThT under blue light.

Both address novelty claims about Gram-negative bacteria (C149, and C24 in peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED regarding ABFDF model advantages. Peer reviewers find the novelty claim UNSUPPORTED, directly contradicting the 'first' claim by citing Hennes et al. (2023) reporting collective electrical oscillations in N. gonorrhoeae.

Partial overlap on reproducibility across conditions (C38-C40 in OpenEval; C38-C40 also in peer R2). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED demonstrating robustness. Peer reviewers' concerns about blue light controls (R2) indirectly question whether the reproducibility reflects intrinsic dynamics or experimental artifacts.

Both address power-law fits and anomalous exponents (C104, C106, C108-C109). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by agreement between model and experiment. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN (in R10), questioning the model-experiment similarity and noting unclear documentation of measurement methods.

OpenEval rates habituation analogy and VBNC speculation (C94-C95, C140-C141, C143) as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging explicit speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval finds K+-based signaling mechanism (C10-C11, C119-C120) SUPPORTED with caveat about 'conserved mechanism' extrapolation. No direct peer review evaluation of these specific claims found, though peer concerns about ThT validity indirectly affect mechanistic interpretations.
OpenEval finds robustness across biofilm morphologies (C58-C60) SUPPORTED by consistent intensity profiles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval finds velocity measurements (C112-C114) SUPPORTED with C114 noted as speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific velocity claims.

OpenEval rates future application predictions (C126, C145-C156) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative extrapolations lacking experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates MS channel-Q channel relationship (C134-C135) as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging complexity beyond current characterization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval finds literature context and background (C1-C29) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Peer review R13 addresses novelty (C24) but not the broader background claims.
